claims.status_note: #13 (fix governance instead of ending the fund), #15 (prefers the Shielded Labs/Tachyon compromise) and #16 ('still too early') argue against ending it; #19 and #22 would vote to end it. Nobody changes position.
claims.text: The Zcash Development Fund should be ended entirely ahead of its scheduled November 2028 termination, rather than eliminating only the ZCG slice and leaving 100% to coinholders.

claims.status_note: No reply addresses the half-measure argument directly; #5 and #12 oppose scrapping ZCG on other grounds.
claims.text: Eliminating ZCG while leaving the whole Dev Fund to coinholders is a half-measure that fails to address taxation without representation, risks consolidating power in one group, shifts leverage and distorts incentives.

claims.status_note: #11 says private funding is not yet plentiful (one Zcash-specific VC has funded one company) and #13 says a new team may have no other path; joshs does not answer either point.
claims.text: The Development Fund has served its purpose: new privately funded teams have arrived, funding is no longer scarce, and the two funds are now valued at more than $300M.

claims.status_note: No reply addresses the incentive argument for coinholder-funded teams; #13 applies an incentives lens to ZODL instead.
claims.text: Teams funded by a quarterly coinholder vote optimize to make the vote go their way; issuance that funds a team is a subsidy, and a subsidy produces teams that serve the subsidy rather than the market.

claims.status_note: #6 replies that the same attack applies to every coinholder vote and asks whether all such votes should then be abolished; joshs does not answer.
claims.text: Stake-based power can be bought: a nation-state could buy ZEC to steer Zcash, as a single actor with a large stake did in Steem, ending in a fork and a loss of decentralization.

claims.status_note: #2 asks who these people are and says the election controversy's allegations were aimed at FPF, not ZCG; #3 says the reports concern past ZCG committees and names no one.
claims.text: The fund structure quells speech: some community members and ZCG funding recipients fear speaking out because funding could be withheld.

claims.status_note: #11 says Zcash has very few private investors, #12 says the proponents have offered no replacement program, and #13 says new teams still need an independent grants path; joshs replies only to #13, on other points (#17).
claims.text: Large holders who want to fund projects can write a check today with the same influence and without the politics, which is a fair free-market model.

claims.status_note: #22 asks how coinholder voting can be taxation without representation; #20 restates the claim without further argument and #26 says whales do not represent him.
claims.text: Coinholder voting on an issuance-funded development fund is taxation without representation: everyone is taxed, but a few large holders choose the winners.

claims.status_note: Nobody replies to #21; #1 gives the same November 2028 expiry date.
claims.text: By default the dev fund keeps accruing until the next halving (around November 2028) and then stops, and the ZCG slice's disbursement can be changed without a protocol change, so the status quo is itself an alternative.

claims.status_note: #10 and #18 discuss what defines consensus, but nobody responds to the prediction itself.
claims.text: If the path is chosen by following the coinholders' decision, as was done when forming NU7, the proposal preferred by a group the poster does not name will definitely win.

claims.status_note: Nobody replies; #1 also opposes eliminating ZCG alone, but for different reasons.
claims.text: ZCG itself should not be scrapped (ending or restructuring the funding is acceptable), and proposals to end it offer no replacement for the innovation platform it provides.

claims.status_note: No reply; #6 puts it partly as a question.
claims.text: Zcash could move to a Bitcoin-style model with node-based freedoms such as UASFs, in which nodes choose whether to contribute to the dev fund and miners may contribute voluntarily, instead of coinholder votes and ZIP-enforced node compliance.

claims.status_note: No reply addresses the call to slow down.
claims.text: There is no emergency: the debate should continue for months until there is broader consensus, rather than being rushed.

claims.status_note: Nobody argues against per-person polling; #19 and #22 still discuss a coinholder vote.
claims.text: Voting weighted by coin amount lets wealth decide outcomes and disenfranchises less wealthy coinholders, so per-person coinholder polling should be added as another input to governance decisions.

claims.status_note: #17 replies that ZODL is not profitable, that ending the fund hurts it financially, and that joshs has taken positions against his own interests; dogemos does not respond in the thread.
claims.text: ZODL is the party that has benefited most from the dev fund and needs it least, so it is structurally misaligned to propose ending the fund while competing with teams that still need it.

claims.status_note: #17 says ZODL took no ECC resources but does not dispute the lineage or the amounts.

claims.text: ZODL's $25M+ seed round was raised on a team, codebase and product that the Dev Fund paid for between 2020 and 2024, and would not have been possible without the fund doing the early, risky part.

claims.status_note: #17 does not address the licensing and branching changes; #25 only appreciates the post.

claims.status_note: Nobody comments on the linked proposal in this thread.

claims.status_note: #21 replies that the status quo is the other option; #15 does not respond.
claims.text: If the interested parties cannot settle on the Shielded Labs/Tachyon compromise, there are not really any other options besides ending the dev fund.

claims.status_note: Nobody disputes or confirms it in the thread.
claims.text: ZODL took no ECC resources and incurred debt before its raise, is not profitable, and is hurt financially by ending the dev fund; joshs refused direct dev funding as ECC CEO and takes positions against his own and his team's interests.

claims.status_note: #23, #24 and #26 argue a coinholder-amount vote cannot show what the community thinks; #19 does not reply.

claims.status_note: No reply to #24.
claims.text: Binding majority-rule voting endangers those outside the majority; polling should be one information input, and decisions made in Zcash's name must ethically include non-coinholders.

claims.status_note: No reply to #24.
claims.text: Those calling for coinholder-amount voting are seeking political power for themselves.

posts.annotation: Proposes ending the Zcash Development Fund entirely before November 2028 rather than only eliminating ZCG, arguing that coinholder-voted funding means taxation without representation, purchasable power, subsidized teams and chilled speech.

Asks who the grantees afraid to speak are; says the election controversy's allegations were aimed at FPF and enforced by the community, not ZCG, and that ZSAs, the main criticism of ZCG, bear many ZODL members' names.

signals.note: Asks for the specific people and views behind the claim that ZCG recipients fear speaking out.
signals.span: Have they? Who are they? Are we aware of them? What views?

posts.annotation: Says he is not accusing anyone: the reports of fear of speaking out concern past, not current, ZCG committees, and the structure is the problem, not the people.

signals.note: Separates the argument about structure from the people involved.
signals.span: I'm not trying to vilify anyone. It's the structure that is the problem.

posts.annotation: Welcomes more options but does not see how a path will be chosen; if coinholders decide as they did for NU7, the proposal 'you know who' prefers will definitely win.
Says scrapping the whole fund is the worst choice; scrapping the funding itself or restructuring is fine, but ZCG itself should not be scrapped.

Asks whether coinholder votes should then be abolished for all decisions on Zcash's direction, since all suffer the same attack; proposes a Bitcoin-style model where nodes and miners choose whether to fund development.
Asks what defines general consensus on Zcash: coinholders alone, or polls across the ecosystem's caucuses.

Supports pausing the Dev Fund if no money is thrown away or reallocated and governance improves (per-person voting, a ZCG ten-year plan); says there is no emergency, the debate needs months, and private funding is not yet plentiful.

signals.note: Attributes the urgency to a deliberately fabricated emergency meant to rush the community, a motive no evidence in the post settles.
signals.span: the energy feels like a fabricated emergency to rush the community into making rash decisions

signals.note: Ascribes to an unnamed group an intent to fabricate consensus in order to throw the money away or take it for themselves.
signals.span: Presuming that the bulls in the china cabinet don't fabricate enough "consensus" to throw that money away or send it to themselves.

posts.annotation: Says he would be convinced if the Winklevosses or Cypherpunk, whom he names as behind the push, opened a formal VC program with a guaranteed annual amount; so far he has seen proposals to kill ZCG, none to replace it.

signals.note: Explains the proposal by a profit motive instead of by anything its proponents said.
signals.span: But so far I've only seen proposals to kill one innovation platform, none to replace it. That convinces me its a pure profit play.

signals.note: Puts an invented, self-serving statement in the mouth of a VC to caricature the proponents' view; no participant said this.
signals.span: "Yeah but I don't want to spend the money, only get the money ZCG being cut gives me. If I open a program I have to give away the money and that's no good :("

posts.annotation: Asks whether the fight is against the fund or its running; argues ZODL, ECC's continuation and the largest dev fund recipient, is structurally misaligned to propose ending it, and that the fix is governance, not ending the fund.

signals.note: Separates the incentive argument from anyone's intentions.
signals.span: My concern isn't anyone's intent. It's incentives.

posts.annotation: Says a proposal most parties including ZCG and maxdesalle agree on has been published, authored by Sean Bowe and posted by zooko, and links it.
Prefers the Shielded Labs/Tachyon proposal to nuking the dev fund, but says that if the interested parties cannot settle on that compromise there are not really any other options.
Believes it is still too early: scaling back is fine, turning the fund off is too radical.

Says he refused direct dev funding as ECC CEO, the raise aimed to remove dependence on the fund and secure legal backing, ZODL took no ECC resources and is unprofitable, so ending the fund hurts it; he argues against his own interest.

signals.note: The author states ZODL's financial interest in the outcome.
signals.span: We are not profitable and ending the dev fund also hurts us financially.

posts.annotation: Says consensus is the view of both coinholders and the caucuses, with one weightier than the other.
Supports ending the fund mainly because taxation should never happen without representation; says a THV would show what the community thinks and expects most who want to keep the fund would agree.
Says coinholder voting for an issuance-based development fund is taxation without representation.
Says the default is that accrual continues until the next halving and then stops, and the ZCG slice's disbursal can be changed without a protocol change, so the status quo is another option.
Asks how coinholder voting can be taxation without representation and how consensus to end the fund would be reached; says he would vote to end it.
Says voting only with money disenfranchises less wealthy coinholders, no country lets people vote with money, and per-person coinholder polling should supplement coinholder-amount polling.

Says voting is not polling and binding majority rule endangers minorities; decisions for Zcash must include non-coinholders; opposes coinholder-amount voting, favors per-person polling, and says its advocates are seeking political power.

signals.note: Ascribes a power-grab motive to everyone calling for coinholder-amount voting.
signals.span: What I have seen from those calling for coinholder-amount voting is a naked political power grab and it's not even a well-disguised one.

signals.note: Imputes an exclusionary hidden meaning to the other side's use of 'everyone'.
signals.span: Unless what you really mean when you say "everyone" is "everyone who I am comfortable being in the same room with."

posts.annotation: Appreciates the reasoning in #13.
Says he is not represented by the whales who determine most coin votes.

open_questions.text: Who are the ZCG funding recipients said to fear speaking out, and what evidence supports the claim?
How should the community decide: a coinholder-amount vote, per-person polling or another method, and what counts as consensus on Zcash?
Does the published compromise proposal, or the Shielded Labs/Tachyon proposal, settle the dispute, or is the status quo the realistic alternative?
Will ZODL respond to the points about its relicensing, private main branch and end of support for the MIT SDKs?

overview.text: joshs of ZODL answers a separate proposal to eliminate ZCG and leave the whole Dev Fund to coinholders. He calls that a half-measure and argues the entire fund should end ahead of its November 2028 expiry, because coinholder-controlled funding is taxation without representation, lets teams optimize for votes, exposes the fund to purchased stake, chills speech and is unnecessary now that private funding exists.

Early replies challenge the details. strahncryptography asks who the grantees afraid to speak are, and joshs says the reports concern past committees and the structure, not people (#2, #3). strahncryptography also asks whether, by joshs's logic, all coinholder votes should be abolished, and opposes scrapping ZCG (#5, #6, #12). artkor and Monsignoree ask how a path will be chosen and what counts as consensus (#4, #10, #18).

emersonian supports pausing the fund only if no money is thrown away or reallocated, calls for per-person polling, says there is no emergency and doubts that private funding is plentiful (#11). dogemos asks whether the target is the fund or how it is run, and argues that ZODL, as ECC's continuation and the largest past recipient, is structurally misaligned to propose ending it (#13). joshs replies that he refused direct dev funding as ECC CEO, took no ECC resources and that ending the fund hurts ZODL too (#17).

Shorter views follow: gigantes prefers the Shielded Labs/Tachyon compromise to nuking the fund (#15), dismad finds ending it too early (#16), and strahncryptography links a published proposal said to have broad agreement (#14). nuttycom notes the default is that accrual continues to the next halving and then stops (#21).

On October 31 thailand85 backs ending the fund and suggests a THV (#19); joshs restates the taxation-without-representation point (#20). thailand85 asks how coinholder voting could be that (#22), and emersonian, fabacab and Milton reply that amount-weighted voting leaves out less wealthy and non-coinholders and that per-person polling is needed (#23, #24, #26).

positions.label: End the Development Fund entirely
positions.summary: The fund has served its purpose and funding is no longer scarce. Coinholder-voted funding amounts to taxation without representation, makes teams optimize for the vote, can be captured by purchased stake and chills speech; large holders can fund projects directly. Eliminating only ZCG is a half-measure, so the whole fund should end before 2028.

positions.label: Keep or scale back the fund and fix how it is run
positions.summary: Ending the fund entirely is premature or the wrong remedy. The concern is incentives and governance, so build a more transparent, neutral system, keep an independent grants path for new teams, or adopt the Shielded Labs/Tachyon compromise instead.

positions.label: Protect ZCG and distrust the push to end it
positions.summary: ZCG should not be scrapped; funding can be ended or restructured. The proponents have offered no replacement program, the claims of chilled speech lack named evidence, and the coinholder-vote attack applies to every coinholder vote.

positions.label: Slow down; other options exist and consensus needs time
positions.summary: There is no emergency, the status quo is itself an option, and it is unclear how a path will be chosen or what counts as consensus. The debate should run for months with better polling before a decision.

positions.label: Weight governance by people, not coin amount
positions.summary: Voting by coin amount lets wealth decide and leaves out less wealthy holders and non-coinholders. Per-person coinholder polling should be added as one input, and a coinholder-amount vote cannot show what the community thinks.

summary.tldr: joshs (ZODL) proposes ending the Zcash Development Fund entirely instead of only eliminating ZCG, arguing coinholder-voted funding is taxation without representation. Replies mostly favor keeping or restructuring it, slowing down, or weighting governance by people rather than coin amount; nobody has changed position.
